_comment: Two ways to connect to the CockroachDB Cloud Managed MCP Server. (1) DEFAULT / what the Cloud Console actually generates (Cluster -> Connect -> MCP integration): no key in the file at all, just the cluster id - the MCP client does an interactive OAuth 2.1 approval in your browser on first connect. Nothing secret ever lives in this file. (2) For headless/automated use (e.g. a CI job or an unattended agent that can't do an interactive OAuth prompt), add an Authorization: Bearer header with a service-account API key instead - see github.com/cockroachdb/claude-plugin for that variant. As of ccloud CLI v0.6.12 (the publicly downloadable build at the time of writing), `ccloud service-account create` is documented but not yet present in that binary; create the service account via the Cloud Console's Service Accounts page instead if you need option (2).
